title: Naturality of normalized tensor-Hom uncurrying on localized chain maps
statement: Let X be a scheme and D(X) its derived category with the recorded tensor and derived internal Hom RHom [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-model]. Let t_{K,L,M}:Hom(K,RHom(L,M)) -> Hom(K tensor L,M) be any family. Write Q for localization, I for the fixed functorial K-injective resolution, j_{L,M}:RHom(QL,QM) -> Q HomComplex(L,I(M)) for the fixed factorization isomorphism, eta_M:M->I(M) for the resolution map, mu(P,L):QP tensor QL->Q Tot(P tensor L) for the localization tensor map, and U(phi):Tot(P tensor L)->I(M) for the explicit componentwise uncurrying [lem-pc-tensor-hom-uncurry-differential]. Assume that for every K-flat complex P and complexes L,M and phi:P->HomComplex(L,I(M)), t_{QP,QL,QM}(Qphi followed by j_{L,M}^{-1}) equals mu(P,L) followed by Q U(phi) followed by (Qeta_M)^{-1}. Also assume that for all derived isomorphisms alpha:Kprime->K, beta:Lprime->L, gamma:M->Mprime and inputs f:K->RHom(L,M), t_{Kprime,Lprime,Mprime}(alpha followed by f followed by RHom(beta,gamma)) equals (alpha tensor beta) followed by t_{K,L,M}(f) followed by gamma. Then for arbitrary complexes P,Pprime,L,Lprime,M,Mprime, actual chain maps a:Pprime->P, b:Lprime->L, c:M->Mprime, and arbitrary derived f:QP->RHom(QL,QM), t_{QPprime,QLprime,QMprime}(Qa followed by f followed by RHom(Qb,Qc)) equals (Qa tensor Qb) followed by t_{QP,QL,QM}(f) followed by Qc. Only the three variable maps are required to be images of chain maps; no extension to arbitrary derived variable maps is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08DJ; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0A90 and 0A96 (read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DJ, /tag/0A90, /tag/0A96)

proof.text: Replace P,Pprime,L,Lprime by K-flat representatives, and M,Mprime by their fixed functorial K-injective resolutions. For the induced morphisms between K-flat representatives, take a common K-flat refinement of each roof denominator. Into the K-injective target, the numerator lifts to a chain map modulo homotopy. Likewise Hom(Lflat,I(M)) is K-injective, so the transported input f has a chain representative phi into this Hom complex. Use hi to express all original values of t through the values on these models.

For model maps alpha,beta,gamma, compare uncurrying of alpha followed by phi followed by Hom(beta,I(gamma)) with tensor(alpha,beta) followed by uncurrying(phi) followed by I(gamma). In total degree n restrict to each summand Pprime^p tensor Lprime^q, p+q=n. The Hom product projection of pre/postcomposition is phi_p projected at q, precomposed by beta_q and postcomposed by I(gamma)_n; alpha_p acts by precomposition. Naturality of the sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction and symmetry give identical evaluations on both sides. Coproduct extensionality gives equality of chain maps. Differential compatibility is supplied by schemeTensorHomUncurryGraded_comm.

Apply Q to the component equality and use ht to substitute each value of t. The functorial resolution augmentation, localization internal-Hom comparison, and lax tensor comparison are natural, so their composites turn the model equality into the displayed equality. A homotopy of representatives yields a homotopy of the uncurried maps: uncurry its degree-minus-one components and use the signed Hom differential formula to show that its boundary is the difference. Thus Q kills that difference. Cancel the common-refinement and replacement isomorphisms using hi. This proves the equation for the specified Q-images of chain maps, without extending to general derived arrows.

proof_origin.place: Tags 08DJ, 0A90, 0A96; component normalization argument restricted to images of chain maps

lean.statement:
theorem tensorHomUncurry_chain_natural (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (t : ∀ K L M : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      (K ⟶ (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
        X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op L, M)) → (K ⊗ L ⟶ M))
    (ht : ∀ (P L M : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ),
        P.IsKFlat →
        ∀ φ : P ⟶ homComplex (R := X.sheaf) L
            ((schemeHomKInjectiveResolution X).obj M),
          t (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)
              (DerivedCategory.Q.map φ ≫
                (schemeDerivedInternalHomResolutionIso X L M).inv) =
            pullbackTensorModelMap X P L ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map (schemeTensorHomUncurry X P L M φ) ≫
                schemeHomResolutionInverse X M)
    (hi : letI := schemeDerivedTensorMonoidal X
    ∀ (K K' L L' M M' : schemeDerivedCategory X)
      (a : K' ≅ K) (b : L' ≅ L) (c : M ≅ M')
      (f : K ⟶ (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
        X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op L, M)),
      t K' L' M' (a.hom ≫ f ≫
        (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map (b.hom.op, c.hom)) =
        (a.hom ⊗ₘ b.hom) ≫ t K L M f ≫ c.hom) :
    letI := schemeDerivedTensorMonoidal X
    ∀ (P P' L L' M M' : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
      (a : P' ⟶ P) (b : L' ⟶ L) (c : M ⟶ M')
      (f : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶
        (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L), DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)),
      t (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P') (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L') (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M')
          (DerivedCategory.Q.map a ≫ f ≫
            (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
              X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map ((DerivedCategory.Q.map b).op,
                DerivedCategory.Q.map c)) =
        (DerivedCategory.Q.map a ⊗ₘ DerivedCategory.Q.map b) ≫
          t (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) f ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map c
